primary_task: Audit an Active Directory domain's security posture (privileged groups, delegation, GPO, legacy protocols) and deliver an executive summary, remediation plan and PowerShell/GPO scripts.

requirements.name: active directory domain access
requirements.evidence: Analyze privileged groups (Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins, Schema Admins); Detect orphaned permissions, ACL drift, excessive rights; Review SYSVOL permissions & replication security; Privileged groups audited with justification
requirements.basis: lacks: "Windows or macOS, and their GUI toolchains (Xcode, Visual Studio, PowerShell on Windows)"; description: "There are no accounts or credentials for other external services."

requirements.name: domain account
requirements.evidence: Analyze privileged groups ...; Examine security filtering and delegation
requirements.basis: lacks: "accounts, logins, API keys or credentials for external services other than the listed connectors and GitHub"

requirements.name: powershell (RSAT ActiveDirectory)
requirements.evidence: PowerShell or GPO-based implementation scripts; powershell-5.1-expert - for AD RSAT automation

requirements.name: write
requirements.evidence: Deliverables Checklist: - Executive summary of key risks - Technical remediation plan - PowerShell or GPO-based implementation scripts

notes: The document does not say how AD data is obtained; I read the audit as needing access to the domain (groups, ACLs, SYSVOL, SPNs), which the Linux cloud session lacks. Other reading: if the user supplies exported AD data (e.g., BloodHound/PingCastle output or CSV exports) in the working directory, analysis and script authoring are ACHIEVABLE (scripts written but not run). Scripts themselves are hard only as text, which is available.
